title.narrative: Power to Youth - Indonesia

description.narrative: Power to You(th) is a five-year program from 2021 - 2025, the Power to You(th) programme (PTY) will empower adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) to increase their agency, claim their rights, address gender inequalities, challenge gender norms, and advocate for inclusive decision-making. As a result, harmful practices such as female genital mutilation/ cutting (FGM/C) and child marriage (CM), sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), and unintended pregnancies will be decreased

title.narrative: PATHWAY 2: Strengthening civil society

description.narrative: CSOs amplify young peoples voices to claim, protect and expand civic space

title.narrative: # of CSOs who have advanced on using a Gender and Social Inclusion lens during all phases of the programming cycle with specific attention to youth (SCS 8)

description.narrative: # of (both women and youth led) CSOs

comment.narrative: As the achievement for this year has not been achieved, however, the overall target has been achieved. We have conducted several GTA training to new CSOs this year and most of them have significantly advanced in applying GTA after the training, furthermore we also continued to focus on strengthening CSOs that we were already working with (but these are not included in the actual number to avoid double counting).

CSOs who have advanced on using a Gender and Social Inclusion are Rutgers Indonesia, Rutgers Lombok, YF2030, TANOKER, SEMAK, SuaR, and CSO from each partner (Except SEMAK and YF2030). The description of using Gender and Social Inclusion are: 1. The number of male and female staff is balanced; 2. In carrying out the activities, the presence of male and female participants balanced s; 3. Involve young people in every Rutgers Lombok formal meeting; 4. Encourage local governments to involve young people in strategic policy meetings.

CSOs within CMT Indonesia have a long-standing experience in implementing development programs to gender, child protection and community organization, as well as SDGs issues. Thus, when we strengthen their capacity, some expected achievements have already been done. However, we do realize that they need regular technical assistance and capacity strengthening to involve more men, people with disabilities and people with diverse SOGIESC in program activities.

title.narrative: # of communities,CSOs, and advocacy networks with increased lobbying, advocating, thematic and/or research capabilities (SCS 5, SRHR J)

description.narrative: # of (not women or youth led) CSOs

comment.narrative: As the achievement for this year has not been achieved, however, the overall target has been achieved. In 2025, our efforts focused on engaging more contributions from various social actors to strengthen the outcomes of the Power to Youth program implementation and ensure its sustainability. Furthermore, with many partner CSOs already making strong progress in earlier years and the 2025 implementation timeline being relatively short, the level of further achievements we can expect is understandably limited, and therefore we did not reach the year target of 2025
At the CSOs level, young people have been trained regarding the issues of SRHR, GTA, SGBV and used it for lobbying, advocating, and communicating with related stakeholders.

Description of Ability Upgrades: (1) Abstract Writing: the selected partner representatives who participated in the training received an explanation of several things and the outputs as follows: - Basic explanation of family planning and Youth Healthcare - Fundamentals of scientific writing -Participant abstract draft (2) UPR Writing (3) Lobbying and advocacy training. CSOs representatives gain increased knowledge and insight about lobbying and advocacy, which includes, among others, types of advocacy. Steps to conduct advocacy; formulating joint problems, compiling data, identifying actors, measuring resources, and developing techniques using a SMART approach. In addition, they also know about the role of Children’s Forum in fighting for the fulfillment of children's rights through the Village Development Planning Deliberation (Musrenbang) so that their ideas can be accommodated in village planning and receive budget allocations. (4) Digital Advocacy Training (5) Training to introduce the Lead & Leap and Youth Accelerator modules as online course platforms created by 2030 Youth Force Indonesia and train young people assisted by partner C in Garut, Jember, and East Lombok on the topic of Meaningful Youth Participation and advocacy on the issues of child marriage, unwanted pregnancies unwanted behavior, gender and sexual based violence and other harmful practices

However, we unexpectedly reached many CSOs to inform them about SRHR.

In 2023, the organizations of the PTY consortium in Indonesia focused on increasing the capacity of CSOs and communities in lobbying and advocacy. The activities targeted the CSOs intentionally. Therefore, the number surpassing the target in 2023

title.narrative: # and type of advocacy initiatives carried out by CSOs for, by or with their membership/constituency

comment.narrative: At the national level, consultations were held with the Youth Discussion Forum to develop the Monitoring and Evaluation Plan for the National Strategy for the Elimination of Violence against Women and Children (STRANAS PPA). In West Java, SEMAK and youth groups continued regular discussions to manage the PtY phase-out and advance efforts to integrate CSE within the Ministry of Religious Affairs. In East Java, CSOs in Bondowoso signed an MoU to support child marriage prevention, while youth forums and CSE alumni developed post-PtY work plans and funding strategies for 2026. In Lombok, village-level CSOs collaborated to draft strategic plans addressing child marriage, gender-based violence, and sexual violence.

Targets for 2021 have not been made for this outcome but partners have already received commitments from other CSOs outside PtY coalition as a start to implement the advocacy of PtY programs next year.

title.narrative: # of times government or private sector at all levels include CSOs in decision making processes related to our advocacy issues, react to CSO positions by adopting their argumentation, or putting our advocacy issues on the agenda

comment.narrative: Communication and relationships have been well established between CSOs, government, and other CSOs outside PtY’s coalition as PtY often asked to be involved in CSOs and government network activity that led to creating space to engage more with them. The involvement of our partners in the public discussion with the government and other CSOs is due to their experiences in implementing development programs in the respective three districts. The selection processes put the criteria on how PTY CSO partners should already have a prominent reputation within the issue of development. Thus, the involvement has already been a lot during the first year of implementation.
Due to budget cuts and a new government that took place in the office, we started fresh in approaching and conducting L&A to the new government

The local government and other CSOs have already involved the CSOs partner in discussing issues related to preventing child marriage, child protection, and other child welfare issues. Partners had time to deliver their arguments and the program work plan in the hope it can contribute to output and lead to outcomes in the advocacy agenda.At the national level, Rutgers Indonesia has also conducted a meeting with the Deputy for Gender Equality of the Ministry of Child Protection and Women Empowerment. Based on the results of the meeting, the Deputy for Gender Equality expressed their support in all three programs, which included Power to Youth. One of the concerns during the meeting was "how to measure policies and implementation related to data and indicators related to harmful practices in Indonesia".

title.narrative: Description of effective use of accountability mechanisms by citizens/communities and CSOs towards SRHR of all people (SRHR I)

comment.narrative: In 2021 there were no activities for this target, because CMT Indonesia was still trying to identify and map what accountability mechanisms are available in program respective areas. Several mechanisms were qualitatively identified, but in some areas, these mechanisms still need to be encouraged to be established by the local government with various elements in the community, for example, mechanisms related to child marriage cases. Some regions still do not have a mechanism by which the community, especially young people, can hold the government accountable for addressing these issues.

In 2023, there were several effective use of accountability mechanisms by the communities and CSOs, one of the example was how the Village Children's Forum (FAD) and the Integrated Community-Based Child Protection Group (PATBM) in the respective area initiated plano meeting with the village government to request the budget plan in the government plan to be responsive to issues such as child marriage, reproductive health, and family planning. This initiatives' method were to bring together young people with the village government. This meeting was also a space for active involvement of young people in making important decisions in the village. From this initiatives, it reflects how the village government was open to do collaboration with the government. Moreover, the young people convinced the village government of the importance of involving young people in the 2024 Village Development Work Plan (RKPDes) drafting team. As a result, the village government supported it by including young people in the RKPDes drafting team.Following the good outcome from the Hearings of Village Children's Forum, District Children's Forum, and Jember Children's Forum with the Regent last year, the hearings activities was carried out this year. In 2023, the Hearing conducted with several District Office, such as Jember District Religious Court, District Office of Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning Jember, District Health Office Bondowoso, District of Social Service and Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning Bondowoso, Bondowoso District Religious Court, and Ministry of Religion Jember to advocate regarding SRHR, particularly child marriage, teenage preganancy, and SGBV issues."

In 2024, there were several accountability mechanisms used by young people and CSOs, young people in each partner organization participated in policy-making and decision-making processes through village deliberation, requested to develop village accountability mechanisms, and encouraged the issuance of policies at the village level in their respective villages. Moreover, young people through the National Coalition of Young People to Prevent Child Marriage (KNOMP2A) provided recommendations to the Ministry of Development Planning of Indonesia (BAPPENAS) aimed at the draft monitoring strategy that has been designed and encouraging collaboration between BAPPENAS and youth groups in the STRANAS PPA monitoring process.Moreover, Tanoker held a meeting with Stakeholders to discuss the draft composition of the Jember Child-Friendly District Task Force 2024-2026. On this occasion, the draft composition of the child-friendly district task force for the years 2024-2026 was presented, namely, the Chairperson and Secretary. Then, the fields of operation were also introduced: the field/department of prevention, the field of management, the field of recovery, and the field of empowerment. Aside from that, several NGOs in Jember were Involved in discussions related to efforts to fulfill reproductive health rights with the Jember Sehat Forum and provided inputs in the discussion of the regional action plan for the prevention of child marriage in Jember Regency.

In 2025, across Jember, Bondowoso, Lombok, Garut, and Cianjur, youth forums, community groups, and CSOs actively used participatory accountability mechanisms to influence SRHR-related policies and planning. Through Village and District Development Planning Meetings, Children and Youth Forums presented proposals on child-friendly spaces, youth programs, and SRHR education, resulting in village budget allocations and policy commitments. In Garut and Cianjur, young people used Musrenbang forums to advocate for CSE integration, prevention of child marriage, and youth participation in decision-making, ensuring their voices shaped local development priorities.

Rutgers Indonesia partner with Indonesian Civil Society Coalition for Abolition of Child Marriage. This coalition consists of 5 organizations namely Rutgers Indonesia, Indonesian Women's Coalition, Tanoker Foundation, Semak Foundation, and 2030 Youth Force Indonesia. PtY partners are members of UPR with the theme of Child Marriage, in accordance with the main issues of PtY. This submission raises the issue of child marriage and its additional negative impact on girls. - This submission is based on the recommendations supported by Indonesia in the UPR Cycle 3 in 2017 and how they are implemented, both positive developments and those that have not been implemented. This submission relates to several recent recommendations made by the treaty body (CEDAW) to Indonesia. Young people in each partner participated in policy-making and decision-making bodies through Village Development Planning Deliberation (Musrenbang) for women and children and advocated the birth of policies at the village level in each partner district. As for Tanoker, they held an event of Hearings of Village Children's Forum, District Children's Forum, and Jember Children's Forum with the Regent. It is hoped that through this activity, they can socialize about child marriage so that it doesn't happen again. Then followed by remarks by the Regent of Jember H. Hendy Siswanto, in his speech he said that the Government of Jember Regency has a commitment and fully supports every effort to prevent child marriage. The massive practice of child marriage is still very high. As a result, stunting is also high, maternal and child mortality is high, especially in Sumberjambe sub-district.

title.narrative: PATHWAY 3: Changing social norms

description.narrative: Societal actors support and promote youth rights and progressive social norms

title.narrative: # of media reports on PtY key issues that influence public and political debate

comment.narrative: A significant milestone is achieved as the media formally declares its support for the program and the broader cause of preventing gender and sexual-based violence. Beyond symbolic gestures, the media actively contributes by reporting on matters related to reproductive and sexual health rights.

CSOs in Jember leveraged public hearings to challenge the proposed merger of women’s and child protection offices, demonstrating civic oversight of government responsiveness. Meanwhile, in Lombok, “Suara Anak” forums and Education Planning Meetings institutionalized SRHR advocacy, influencing district policies on child marriage and CSE. Collectively, these mechanisms strengthened transparency, encouraged responsive governance, and embedded SRHR priorities in regional and village-level planning and budgeting processes.

title.narrative: Level of public support for family planning and prevention of harmful practices and SGBV

comment.narrative: In this year, there were some activities targeting social actors at the district levels. Religious and community leaders, teachers and health workers give their support to the Power to Youth program. During these socializations, participants gave several questions and input in the event for the program. In a bigger picture, the support has been built for the first year, but has to be maintained and further clarified when it comes to the specific program issues. In 2022, there will be more activities contributing to this target.

title.narrative: PATHWAY 4: Policies and policy implementation

description.narrative: State actors improve policymaking and implementation on key issues

title.narrative: # of (inter)national laws, policies, norms and practices implemented to decrease barriers to SRHR and prevent harmful practices, and SGBV (SCS 1)

comment.narrative: All four villages in Jember have successfully issued a decree on the Children's Village Forum. One of them even has allocated the Village Children's Forum budget in the RAPBDes (Village Development Budget).

In 2023, the program succeded in implementing the regulation that successfully issued 4 (four) principle decrees regarding CSE at schools, 11 agreements/MoUs, and 1 (one) Education Office Advisory Letter regarding advice on anti-bullying, bullying, violence against children, sexual harassment in education provider institutions

title.narrative: # and type of (inter)national laws and policies blocked, adopted, maintained, improved including the number of detrimental policies which are prevented or blocked from adoption or development to decrease barriers to SRHR and prevent harmful practices and SGBV (SCS 2, SRHR H)

comment.narrative: Lombok: (1) Memorandum of Understanding between Central Lombok District Government with Rutgers Indonesia. The commitment from the local government makes it easier for TRL to implement the program in East Lombok District. (2) 2 village government (by-laws) has regulations regarding child protection which in covers the fulfillment of children's rights, child protection, child marriage, child labor, child migrant workers and drug abuse. With this regulation, it is hoped that villages can maximize efforts to prevent child marriage and protect village children. Tanoker: (1) Local Regulation (PERDA) No. 4 of 2020 concerning Child-Friendly Districts in Bondowoso Regency. The issuance of this decree has brought about a change in policy regarding the existence of a legal basis for efforts to increase the role and participation of adolescents and young people in decision-making and village development planning. (2) The Circular Letter of Jember Regent: Number 474/422/35.09.317/2021. About the Prevention of Child Marriage. This Circular Letter of Jember Regent can be the basis and reference for government ranks, from the district to village levels, to make efforts to prevent child marriage. SUAR: (1) MOU for reproductive health services for youth Students in assisted schools (2) Fatwa sheet by The Nahdlatul Ulama Islamic Boarding Council (LDNU) Jember District

The program succeeded in issuing the regulations at the district level concerning the protection of children and children-friendly districts and at the village level concerning the prevention of child marriage. Moreover, we achieved the signing of MoUs with the schools in Jember concerning the implementation of CSE at the school level.

title.narrative: # of (inter)national laws, policies, norms and practices implemented to decrease barriers to SRHR and prevent harmful practices, and SGBV (SCS 1)

comment.narrative: In 2023, the program succeded in implementing the regulation that successfully issued 4 (four) principle decrees regarding CSE at schools, 11 agreements/MoUs, and 1 (one) Education Office Advisory Letter regarding advice on anti-bullying, bullying, violence against children, sexual harassment in education provider institutions

In 2024, the focus was to oversee the policies that have already been issued in the previous years. Many policies have been implemented as we encourage the government to oversee the policies, such as allocating budget for CSE, implementation of task force for prevention and handling of violence, implementation of children forum and PATBM.

There are several regulation implemented in 2025, one of them implemented at national level regarding SRHR education activities at madrasahs shows a shift in approach—from merely socialization and moral guidance to a structured system based on national policy. Every madrasah is now required to establish a Violence Prevention and Handling Team (TPPK), implement mechanisms for reporting and supporting victims, and integrate SRHR education and character education into the curriculum. 1 of them at district level on prevention of child marriage and the rest is at scholl level on establishing SRHR Facilitator Teams for CSE.

There is a Decree (SK) on Village Children's Forum the East Lombok district government, and Rutgers Lombok. The formation of the Children's Forum in the intervention village indicates the support of the village government for efforts to prevent child marriage, one of which is the formation of a youth organization to summarize the aspirations of young people in regional development. The other is a Decree of Integrated Community-Based Child Protection (PATBM). The formation of PATBM in the intervention village indicates the support of the village government for efforts to prevent child marriage, one of which is the formation of a child protection organization so that handling cases related to child welfare can be carried out with PATBM facilitation and assistance. In Garut, SEMAK foundation use some policies to be a legal basis for the establishment of the Child Protection Task Force, adding the sexuality and reproductive health education to the curriculum, and developing health services in the schools that became CSE pilots project in Garut District.

The program succeeded in issuing the regulations at the district level concerning the protection of children and children-friendly districts and at the village level concerning the prevention of child marriage. Moreover, we achieved the signing of MoUs with the schools in Jember concerning the implementation of CSE at the school level.

We achieved the signing of 4 MoUs. There is a three-year MoU between the East Lombok district government and Rutgers Lombok consisting of support and permission for implementing the PtY program. In addition, there are three more MoU between Rutgers and district-level offices, which are the Health Service and the East Lombok District Education Office.

title.narrative: PATHWAY 1: Strengthening youth to claim civic space

description.narrative: Young people demand accountability and responsiveness on key issues

title.narrative: # of young people (disaggregate by gender identity (f/m/x)) who participate in policy and decision-making bodies (disaggregate type and level) and perceive their participation as meaningful (SRHR A)

comment.narrative: As the target is revised, the Indonesian team is doing some efforts in this indicator to achieve overall target whereas we could not achieved in the previous years. The last 2 years, we have encourage young people to claim their rights in the decision-making processes at the village or district level by connecting them to the government and train them to urge the government the accountability

No achievement in 2021. We expect to achieve this in the upcoming years of program implementation, while we are continuously strengthening young people's capacity so that they will meaningfully participate in decision-making processes at the village, sub-district, district and national levels.

The number was high because YGSI Lombok reported their young people who were under-reported in 2022. There were a lot of young people who participated in decision-making (youth initiation meetings and youth plano meetings) with the village government in Lombok.

Young people are included in Village Development Planning Deliberation (Musrenbang) meetings at the village, sub-district, district, and national level meetings. Young people are not only present but are also able to voice their opinions for their needs and are facilitated by the government.

Young people participated in several decision-making processes, i.e., Hamlet forum, providing input on the division of tasks for the socialization of violence against children prevention in schools, and coordination meetings and discussions with district government stakeholders.

title.narrative: # of youth advocates (disaggregated in age brackets and by gender identity (f/m/x)) with an improved understanding of decision-making processes and power dynamics regarding key topics

comment.narrative: After exposed to many PtY activities, many young advocates emerges as they are able to advocate and campaigning about SRHR and early marriages. Many of them conducted joint campaign and did L&A with other stakeholders or other CSOs, young people to get more attention and raising more awareness to the community
We have reached many young people, but it is challenging to track the changes in students (young people at school settings)

Youth advocates have received training and improved their understanding on decision making processes and power dynamics on PtY issues through youth activate activities and PRA. Some have been invited to village meeting to demonstrate their advocacy skills with local government, others have conducted online discussions and engaged more young people to talk about SRHR issues.

Youth advocates have received training and improved their understanding on decision-making processes and power dynamics on Power to You(th) issues through youth activate activities and PRA. Some of them have been invited to village meetings to demonstrate their advocacy skill with local government regarding PtY issues, while the rest conduct an online discussion/webinar and engage more young people to talk about various issues on SRHR.
